DEMOCRACY NOW: "World Cup Kicks Off in Mexico Amid Protests Against Austerity and Forced Disappearances"
June 11, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Democracy Now treats the protests as legitimate grievance amplification, not nuisance. Names the 2007 pension privatization the CNTE wants repealed. Names the 130,000 disappeared as a Calderón-era inheritance, not a Sheinbaum failure. Names Peña Nieto as the president who chose to bid for this tournament.

🇲🇽 José Luis Granados Ceja centers the actual ticket scandal — "the people who love this sport are not going to be able to attend." A US outlet covering Mexican social movements without an "expert" demanding militarization is rare enough to warrant the green.

• "The people who love this sport are not going to be able to attend the games"
• Frames 130k disappeared as Calderón's militarized-drug-war legacy
• Mothers of the disappeared adapted Panini stickers with photos of the missing

US EMBASSY / MEX NEWS DAILY: Ambassador Johnson posts on X that US transferred "313 wanted criminals" to Mexico
June 16, 2026 | 🟡

📰 US Ambassador Ronald Johnson uses X to claim 313 criminals transferred under Trump — landing the same week Trump trashes Sheinbaum at the G7. No formal extradition paperwork cited; "transferred" is doing a lot of lifting where the word "extradited" would be testable.

🇲🇽 Mexico's receipts from Foreign Minister Velasco: of 269 extradition requests sent to the US since January 2018, 36 were denied, 233 remain pending, zero fulfilled — while Mexico handed over 90+ organized-crime transfers in the opposite direction.

• Sheinbaum: "Why haven't they handed anyone over?"
• Mexico's tally: 0 of 269 extradition requests fulfilled by US since 2018
• Embassy's preferred channel for diplomatic correction: Elon's website

BREITBART: "Trump at G7: 'Cartels Control Mexico'"
June 18, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Breitbart runs Trump's G7 jab at Sheinbaum verbatim: "good woman but a scared woman." Zero Mexican response. Zero data on the homicide drop. Trump's "90% decrease in water smuggling" stat passes through unverified.

🇲🇽 Mexico's May homicide rate was the lowest in 11 years (47.3/day, down 27.6% YoY) — a number the "cartels totally running Mexico" framing requires its audience never see.

• "The cartels control Mexico, and it's sad"
• "She's a very good woman, but a very scared woman"
• "Mexico has lost control of their country"

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>FED HOLDS RATES 4TH STRAIGHT TIME, FLAGS POSSIBLE HIKE — PESO HOLDS 17.19</u>

The Fed kept rates at 3.50%-3.75% for the fourth consecutive meeting but signaled a possible hike before year-end as US inflation runs at a 3-year high. Mexican peso closed at 17.1929, down just 0.06% on the day — Banxico already concluded its cutting cycle at 6.50% in May. The empire's central bank flailing between stagflation and politics, Mexico's macro discipline absorbing the shock without panic. AMLO's institutional firewall plus Sheinbaum's continuity = Mexican markets holding the line while Powell runs out of room.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SUPREMA CORTE UNANIMOUSLY REJECTS GOOGLE AMPARO IN MONOPOLY CASE</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court unanimously denied Google's amparo against the antimonopoly law that requires document delivery in 10 business days for competition investigations. Reporting Minister Irving Espinosa Betanzo: "The norm is constitutional, as its purpose rests in constitutional Article 28, which imposes on the State the duty to investigate and sanction monopolistic practices with efficiency." The case stems from a 2022 probe into Google's mobile app payments and digital content monopoly — a million-dollar fine already pending. Big Tech can't buy itself out of Mexican law the way it routinely buys US regulators.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MORENA SETS STRICTER RULES THAN PT/PVEM FOR 2027 GUBERNATURAS</u>

Morena candidates must resign public office before competing, can't use social programs to campaign, face anti-nepotism and billboard limits — PT and PVEM, the coalition partners, have none of these restrictions. Registration runs June 22-27 at WTC CDMX for 17 governor races. Morena leader Ariadna Montiel framed it: "These are Morena rules" — not a coalition rupture, just discipline the others won't share. The party born in the streets keeping the bar higher than its allies — the AMLO DNA still showing while the old clientelism creeps back through the PT/PVEM doors.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>CNDH: PEMEX HOSPITAL FORCED INDUCTION, 8-HOUR DELAY, OBSTETRIC VIOLENCE</u>

CNDH Recommendation 22/2026 documents obstetric violence and dehumanizing treatment of a pregnant woman with multiple risk factors at Pemex's Consultorio Reforma (Chiapas) and Hospital Regional de Villahermosa (Tabasco): 8 hours from membrane rupture to delivery, labor induction without consent, no specialized studies, no trained staff. Seven public servants implicated. Pemex hospitals serve oil workers and their families — the institution that built modern Mexico, gutted by decades of neoliberal underinvestment, now failing the people it was built to serve. Energy sovereignty has to include health sovereignty.

🇲🇽🔥 <u>EDOMEX MAYOR FAKED HER OWN KIDNAPPING TO STEAL 40 MILLION PESOS</u>

Tenancingo mayor Nancy Nápoles Pacheco simulated her own abduction to extract 40 million pesos from municipal funds — money meant to cover an embezzlement during her administration — according to the FGJ-Edomex. Her husband and brother-in-law allegedly planned the false kidnapping starting in February; three accomplices already detained, arrest warrants out for the family. State prosecutors didn't bury it. The corruption playbook hasn't changed in Mexican politics — the appetite to expose it has.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>VANCE: US "RESERVES THE RIGHT" TO MILITARY ACTION IN MEXICO</u>

VP JD Vance told Univision the US "reserves the right" to strike cartels inside Mexico — refusing to commit to Sheinbaum's sovereignty red line. "If a cartel has a massive shipment of weapons and fentanyl about to enter the US, of course we'd pursue it," he said, framing intervention as defense of "the American people." 80% of Mexicans reject US military action; Sheinbaum has called sovereignty "not optional, not negotiable." The empire keeps the threat warm. Mexico's answer is the same as it was in 1847, 1914, and 1916.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>MEXICAN CRUDE CRASHES TO $73.05 — UNDER HACIENDA'S 2026 FLOOR</u>

The Mezcla Mexicana closed Tuesday at $73.05 per barrel, down 6% from Monday and the lowest since March 4, putting it 5.4% below the $77.3 baseline baked into the Pre-Criterios Generales de Política Económica 2027. SHCP estimates each $1 swing equals about 9.6 billion pesos in petroleum income; the YTD average sits at $81.94 (still 6% above plan), but the slide tracks the US-Iran Hormuz memorandum that crushed the geopolitical risk premium overnight. "The MOU significantly reduced the probability of immediate disruption," Rystad's Jorge León told El Financiero. Pemex's $80B debt now meets a slimmer fiscal cushion right as Sheinbaum doubles down on autosuficiencia energética — Manzanillo 357MW just came online Friday.
